problem: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) research was growing quickly but was scattered across methods and benchmarks, with no organized Chinese-language overview of its challenges, methods and trends.
motivation: VLN is a representative task in vision-language interaction, and grounding language instructions in visual perception for autonomous navigation is hard. A structured review is needed to compare typical solutions and point out future directions. Only the abstract was available, so details beyond it are not captured.
key_idea: Survey VLN by its core challenges (cross-modal alignment, semantic understanding and reasoning, generalization), then categorize methods into imitation learning, reinforcement learning, self-supervised learning and other methods, and discuss trends.
insight: The abstract frames VLN progress around three core challenges and four learning paradigms. It identifies continuous-environment navigation, complex instruction comprehension and common-sense reasoning as the current trends. It names 3D VLN, embodied question answering and interactive question answering as future directions. No ablations, since this is a survey.
method: Task and challenges: introduces the VLN task and analyzes three challenges: cross-modal semantic alignment, semantic understanding and reasoning, and generalization enhancement.
Datasets and metrics: lists commonly used VLN datasets and evaluation metrics.
Method taxonomy: summarizes progress under imitation learning, reinforcement learning, self-supervised learning and other methods, and compares the effects of typical solutions.
Trends: discusses continuous environment navigation, advanced complex instruction comprehension and common-sense reasoning.
Future directions: 3D VLN, embodied question answering, interactive question answering.
numbers_note: abstract only; survey with no own experiments
results: A survey with no original experimental results. It compares typical VLN solutions across imitation, reinforcement and self-supervised learning, and outlines trends and future directions.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the detailed content is not captured.
Published in 2022, so it predates LLM-based and other more recent VLN work.
